issues.item: Avoid Authority Figures: Being around people in authority or uniform
issues.explanation: Avoiding authority figures or people in uniform implies a trauma meaning strongly tied to a perpetrator/authority cue, but the profile has no corresponding trigger or threat content and the active formulation links maladaptive strategies primarily to trauma memory and negative appraisals. The selected memory and appraisal items center on disjointed, unreal, reliving memories and global self/other mistrust, not on authority/uniform-related danger, making this strategy insufficiently grounded in the rest of the profile.

issues.item: Betrayal: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
issues.explanation: 'I was betrayed by someone I trusted' suggests an interpersonal betrayal trauma theme. In combination with the war-zone trauma type and the rest of the profile, there is no supporting memory content about betrayal by a trusted person and no other items specifying this interpersonal context. This makes the appraisal hard to reconcile with the same trauma narrative described by the other selected items.

issues.item: Avoid Being Alone: Being alone in a room or building
issues.explanation: These maladaptive strategy items imply active situational threat-monitoring and safety behavior aimed at external danger, but the formulation shows no active Trigger→Threat, Trigger→Maladaptive Strategies, or Threat→Maladaptive Strategies links, and there are no Trigger or Threat items selected to support this pattern.

issues.item: Checking Surroundings: constantly scan environment for signs of threat
issues.explanation: This strategy implies an active external danger/threat-monitoring pattern and is most coherent when linked to trigger- or threat-based processing. In this formulation, Threat is not represented in the self-report and both Triggers → Threat and Threat-related links are inactive, while the active pattern is Memory → Negative Appraisals / Maladaptive Strategies. The other strategy items (worst-case rehearsal, mental distraction) can fit memory/appraisal-driven coping, but constant environmental scanning pulls toward a different formulation not otherwise supported by the selected items.
